editorial.headline: Infrastructure Finance, Open Nationally and Clear of Bali’s PMA Moratorium
editorial.standfirst: Conventional infrastructure finance is nationally open to full foreign ownership, and its higher-risk Large-scale profile keeps it outside Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
Conventional infrastructure finance is the business of putting capital behind infrastructure projects: direct lending, refinancing infrastructure previously financed by another party, and subordinated loans connected to infrastructure funding. It is a defined financing activity rather than a general advisory mandate. The enterprise at its centre is an infrastructure-finance company operating on a conventional basis, with the work anchored in the provision of funds to infrastructure projects.

Its scope can extend beyond the core loan book. In support of that business, an infrastructure-finance company may provide credit enhancement, advisory services, equity investment, and assistance in finding a swap market connected to infrastructure financing. It may also provide other related activities or facilities, but those require approval from the Financial Services Authority. That distinction matters: the record presents these as supporting capabilities of the infrastructure-finance business, not as a free-standing promise that every associated service is automatically available.

Registration is open across the full scale range: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. At the national level, the activity is open to foreign investment, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. In plain terms, the national position allows full foreign ownership for this activity. The scale range also makes clear that the classification is not confined to a single size of operator, even though the substance of the activity remains infrastructure financing.

Bali’s position is also comparatively direct. The province permanently blocks PMA registration for activities assessed as Low or Medium-Low risk across the island. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium: at the Large scale, its OSS risk is Medium-High or High. A foreign investor can therefore register this activity in Bali today; the Bali record does not impose a separate foreign-ownership cap or partnership condition. The useful reading is not that Bali creates a special exception, but that this activity sits outside the moratorium’s Low and Medium-Low risk boundary.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today because its Large-scale risk profile sits outside the provincial PMA moratorium.
